It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival on Ice,” on Steam, https://store.steam,com/app/1112480 while you read my thoughts. The game started with a bang as you set foot onto the colony planet. The ground was black as coal, the view was empty and you were all by yourself. As the timer got shorter and the planet got colder you needed to make decisions about what to do to survive. I had four objectives that I needed to meet, each requiring different things to be done to accomplish and you were brought in after the group I had chosen for travel shattered upon entering the planet. There were three teams and I wanted to join forces. When making my group decisions, I placed weight on what the people wanted to play and I asked for their commitment to completing the whole game. There were several new things about this game and I liked that the first thought was to survive. In Survival of the Fittest, before beginning the game we discussed how many resources would be needed and how fast. “Survival on Ice” started by leaving six items on the map in random spots and then just me, two other survivors and the game timer started. To survive I chose Dr. Doomber which had a 3.7 rating and was a great pick of the day. With my skills and items I started out with fire and first things first I was going towards the fire some time before I needed but I had energy and wouldn’t die for a while. Dr. Doomber has a health harvest skill that increased my energy every 10 seconds and a super cold weapon attack, which I used later in the game on a bear. As the time was ticking away and things all got real on the planet. Even when I got food I had to deal with the fact that each time I harvest something it shrinks the resources. This game asks you time and time to make a decision. I was fighting wolves, trying to make it to the shelter, gathering resources, collecting water from puddles and moving in a team to hunt a bear. I had to set my goals so that was easy thing to do but time was ticking and the question of how quickly I was going to kill the bear. I knew what I needed to do and how I had to do it. My time was 7:01 and after 15 minutes of my game I made it to the shelter, collected a couple of items that would help me next day and then returned back to the other two survivors at their camp and collected some supplies, but not the resources i needed to survive. I had wasted too much time and I was now too late. At the time the gas meter was about two bars away from disappearing. They assigned thousands of books the wrong subjects. So, Dr. Cohen began work on an alternate system that she and her partner (a librarian)  have now patented: http://www.amazon.com/Doctor-Doctors-Dont-Kill-Kinds-Ebook/dp/059117724X/ref=sr_1_1_titl…  This seems like another way to help the government and librarians by having better things classified and therefore better results returned in any search.
